A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RRGP-UCB study despite the revised title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on synthetic functions and silicon carrier-lifetime data, including uncontrollable-input experiments in Appendix D.2, with results averaged over 100 simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results, with the uncontrollable-input experiments now discussed in Section 5.2.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an optional approximation using the minimum and maximum robustness values across S posterior sample paths for measures outside the tabulated cases. The central RRGP-UCB algorithm and beta sampling distribution remain unchanged; the approximation is not reported as used in the experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 2D, 4D, and 6D synthetic functions and carrier-lifetime data using EXP, PTR, and EXP-MAE objectives. The uncontrollable-input experiments move from v1 Appendix D.2 to v2 Section 5.2 without expanding coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same nine methods, including Random, US, BQ, BPT-UCB, BBBMOBO, Proposed, and their fixed-parameter variants. Renaming '(fix)' to '(fixed)' and explaining overlapping EXP curves do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The grids, surrogate kernels, noise settings, initialization, instantaneous-regret metric, and experimental procedures are retained. Synthetic and carrier-lifetime experiments still use 300 and 500 iterations, respectively.

E4.justification: The fixed-parameter comparisons, surrogate-mismatch scenarios, and uncontrollable-input tests are retained. The new Appendix D.2 supplies a mathematical equivalence argument, not an additional empirical ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 100 simulations with error bars representing twice the standard error. Figure 1 also retains its sampling count and 95% interval; no new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The matched benchmark plots retain the same regret curves and performance findings. Appendix D.2 newly reports that the EXP experiments had no tied UCB maximizers, a limited qualitative finding supporting the equivalence discussion.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a derivation showing that BBBMOBO (fixed) and Proposed (fixed) select the same points for expectation optimization when the UCB maximizer is unique. The principal regret bounds are retained; v2 Theorems 4.5 and 4.6 reproduce results already present as v1 Theorems B.1 and B.2.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contribution statements retain the same claims: randomized beta selection, expected-regret guarantees for robustness optimization, extensions to continuous and uncontrollable settings, and competitive empirical performance. The revision does not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 and the conclusion explicitly acknowledge that continuous-space extensions require beta to grow with time and involve difficult kernel-dependent constants. Section 4 also expands discussion of latest-iterate versus selected-iterate guarantees and the different dependence of high-probability bounds on time and delta.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 retains the function-generation formulas, environmental distributions, acquisition-function specifications, and hyperparameters, including beta = 9 for fixed variants. No additional implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tay et al. (2022, 2024) and discusses their approximation and Thompson-sampling approaches and regret guarantees. It also clarifies its relationship to Inatsu et al. (2024a), while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, theoretical discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The title and notation are refined, a main-text extensions subsection is introduced, and the uncontrollable-input experiments are integrated into Section 5.

P2.justification: v2 adds the notation table and a separate pseudocode display for the existing finite uncontrollable case. Figures and tables are relocated, experimental captions explain coincident EXP curves, and Figure 1 changes a curve color; the benchmark panels themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability and qualification through revised exposition, the notation table, the equivalence proof, and explicit continuous-space limitations. The main guarantees and experimental evidence remain essentially unchanged. The new sampled-bound approximation lacks validation or a demonstrated connection to condition (3.2), limiting that addition, but the clearer explanations support a modest overall improvement.
